sn36.21:1.1: On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Rajagaha in the Bamboo Grove, the Squirrel Sanctuary.
sn36.21:1.2: Then the wanderer Moḷiyasīvaka approached the Blessed One and exchanged greetings with him.
sn36.21:1.3: When they had concluded their greetings and cordial talk, he sat down to one side and said to the Blessed One:
sn36.21:1.4: “Master Gotama, there are some ascetics and brahmins who hold such a doctrine and view as this:
sn36.21:1.5: ‘Whatever a person experiences, whether it be pleasant or painful or neither-painful-nor-pleasant, all that is caused by what was done in the past.’
sn36.21:1.6: What does Master Gotama say about this?”
sn36.21:2.1: “Some feelings, Sīvaka, arise here originating from bile disorders: that some feelings arise here originating from bile disorders one can know for oneself,
sn36.21:2.3: and that is considered to be true in the world.
sn36.21:2.4: Now when those ascetics and brahmins hold such a doctrine and view as this,
sn36.21:2.5: ‘Whatever a person experiences, whether it be pleasant or painful or neither-painful-nor-pleasant, all that is caused by what was done in the past,’
sn36.21:2.6: they overshoot what one knows by oneself and they overshoot what is considered to be true in the world.
sn36.21:2.7: Therefore I say that this is wrong on the part of those ascetics and brahmins.
sn36.21:3.1: “Some feelings, Sīvaka, arise here originating from phlegm disorders …
sn36.21:3.3: originating from an imbalance of the three …
sn36.21:3.5: produced by careless behaviour … caused by assault … produced as the result of kamma:
sn36.21:3.7: that some feelings arise here produced as the result of kamma one can know for oneself,
sn36.21:3.10: and that is considered to be true in the world.
sn36.21:3.12: Now when those ascetics and brahmins hold such a doctrine and view as this,
sn36.21:3.13: ‘Whatever a person experiences, whether it be pleasant or painful or neither-painful-nor-pleasant, all that is caused by what was done in the past,’
sn36.21:3.14: they overshoot what one knows by oneself and they overshoot what is considered to be true in the world.
sn36.21:3.15: Therefore I say that this is wrong on the part of those ascetics and brahmins.”
sn36.21:4.1: When this was said, the wanderer Moḷiyasīvaka said to the Blessed One:
sn36.21:4.3: Magnificent, Master Gotama!… From today let Master Gotama remember me as a lay follower who has gone for refuge for life.”
sn36.21:5.4: With kamma result as the eighth.
